post.description:
This API endpoint allows authorized client applications to obtain an access token using their Application credentials. The access token is required to authenticate and authorize requests to other Typeface AI API endpoints. 

**Token Expiration & Renewal**:  Access tokens are valid for one hour.

To maintain uninterrupted access to Typeface AI APIs, client applications should implement a mechanism to:
  - *Periodically Refresh*: Automatically fetch a new access token before
  the current one expires.
  - *Error-Based Refresh*: Fetch a new access token when encountering a 401
  Unauthorized error, indicating token expiration.

/profile-service/accounts/{accountId}/pr.description:
`ref` Field Usage in API Responses:

The `ref` field plays a crucial role in the identification and processing of assets across our content generation APIs. It acts as a unique asset identifier that can be leveraged in subsequent API requests. Whenever an API requires asset information within its payload, the ref value from the response should be provided to reference the specific asset.

This field ensures seamless asset integration across various operations, enabling efficient consumption and interaction with assets in our system. Make sure to include the ref field in all relevant requests to facilitate proper asset handling and processing in connected APIs

This API allows you to upload image in the brand kit of given style type. There are two different options available to do so:
  - `content`: The binary format content of image to be uploaded
  - `contentUrl`: Publicly accessible url of the required image

**Sample curl request**
```bash
  curl --silent --location 'https://api-us.typeface.ai/profile-service/accounts/accountId/brand-kits/brandKitId/style-types/image/styleType/images' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  --form 'contentUrl="image url..."'
```

**Note**: It is mandatory to train a Brand-kit image style before it can be utilized in content generation.

post.description:
Creates one or more tags in a single request. Each tag in the request is processed independently, so some tags may succeed while others fail. The response contains a per-item result for every tag in the request, each marked with `success: true` or `success: false`.

For each tag, provide a `name` and `displayName`. Optionally include `parentId` to nest the tag under an existing parent, and `properties` to attach metadata such as `description`. Tags without a `parentId` are created as top-level tags.

The top-level `success` field in the response is `true` only when every tag was created successfully. If any tag fails, `success` is `false` (partial success).

post.description:
Search for tags within an account. Use this to browse the tag taxonomy, find tags by name, or list tags filtered by status.

- **`query`** — Filters tags by name or display name. Searching for a parent tag also returns all of its descendants. When omitted or empty, all tags are returned.
- **`status`** — Filters tags by status (`ACTIVE`, `INACTIVE`, `DEPRECATED`, `REJECTED`, `PENDING`). Defaults to `ACTIVE`. Set to `PENDING` to list newly discovered tag candidates awaiting review.
- **`limit`** / **`cursor`** — Use cursor-based pagination for large result sets.

Each tag in the response includes:
- `fullPath` — a `::` delimited path of tag names from root to the tag (e.g., `marketing::social_media::instagram`).
- `pathIds` — an ordered list of tag IDs matching each segment in `fullPath` (e.g., `[100, 101, 103]`).

These fields let you reconstruct the full hierarchy position of any tag.

The examples below assume a tag hierarchy: **Marketing > Social Media > Instagram**.

#### List all active tags
```json
{
  "limit": 20
}
```

#### Response
```json
{
  "tags": [
    {
      "id": 100,
      "name": "marketing",
      "displayName": "Marketing",
      "ref": "eyJhY2NvdW50...",
      "parentId": null,
      "status": "ACTIVE",
      "description": "Marketing related content",
      "fullPath": "marketing",
      "pathIds": [100],
      "createdAt": "2026-01-15T10:00:00Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-01-15T10:00:00Z",
      "createdBy": "user-1",
      "modifiedBy": "user-1"
    },
    {
      "id": 101,
      "name": "social_media",
      "displayName": "Social Media",
      "ref": "eyJhY2NvdW50...",
      "parentId": 100,
      "status": "ACTIVE",
      "description": "Social media related content",
      "fullPath": "marketing::social_media",
      "pathIds": [100, 101],
      "createdAt": "2026-01-15T10:35:00Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-01-15T10:35:00Z",
      "createdBy": "user-1",
      "modifiedBy": "user-1"
    },
    {
      "id": 103,
      "name": "instagram",
      "displayName": "Instagram",
      "ref": "eyJhY2NvdW50...",
      "parentId": 101,
      "status": "ACTIVE",
      "description": "Instagram specific content",
      "fullPath": "marketing::social_media::instagram",
      "pathIds": [100, 101, 103],
      "createdAt": "2026-01-16T09:00:00Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-01-16T09:00:00Z",
      "createdBy": "user-1",
      "modifiedBy": "user-1"
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": "....."
}
```

#### Search for a tag and its descendants
Searching for `Social Media` returns the matching tag and all tags nested under it (e.g., `Instagram`).
```json
{
  "query": "Social Media",
  "limit": 20
}
```

#### Response
```json
{
  "tags": [
    {
      "id": 101,
      "name": "social_media",
      "displayName": "Social Media",
      "ref": "eyJhY2NvdW50...",
      "parentId": 100,
      "status": "ACTIVE",
      "description": "Social media related content",
      "fullPath": "marketing::social_media",
      "pathIds": [100, 101],
      "createdAt": "2026-01-15T10:35:00Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-01-15T10:35:00Z",
      "createdBy": "user-1",
      "modifiedBy": "user-1"
    },
    {
      "id": 103,
      "name": "instagram",
      "displayName": "Instagram",
      "ref": "eyJhY2NvdW50...",
      "parentId": 101,
      "status": "ACTIVE",
      "description": "Instagram specific content",
      "fullPath": "marketing::social_media::instagram",
      "pathIds": [100, 101, 103],
      "createdAt": "2026-01-16T09:00:00Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-01-16T09:00:00Z",
      "createdBy": "user-1",
      "modifiedBy": "user-1"
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": "....."
}
```

#### List newly discovered tag candidates (pending review)
Tags with `PENDING` status are auto-discovered tags that have not yet been approved or rejected. Use this to power editorial review and governance workflows.
```json
{
  "status": "PENDING",
  "limit": 50
}
```

#### Response
```json
{
  "tags": [
    {
      "id": 215,
      "name": "bedroom_pop",
      "displayName": "Bedroom Pop",
      "ref": "eyJhY2NvdW50...",
      "parentId": 100,
      "status": "PENDING",
      "description": "Lo-fi pop music produced in home studios",
      "fullPath": "marketing::bedroom_pop",
      "pathIds": [100, 215],
      "createdAt": "2026-02-08T14:30:00Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-02-08T14:30:00Z",
      "createdBy": "user-1",
      "modifiedBy": "user-1"
    }
  ],
  "nextCursor": "cursor-abc123"
}
```

patch.description:

Common use cases include renaming a tag, deactivating it, updating its description, or approving / rejecting a pending tag candidate (set status to `ACTIVE` to approve, `REJECTED` to reject).

:information_source: Maximum number of Image variations(`simple_image`) one can generate is capped at 4.

This API is asynchronous and returns immediately after accepting the request. You can use the `batchJobStatus` link for monitoring the status of the Generation Job.

An example of bulk generation is available [here](#bulk-generation) to generate multiple contents at once

---
## Simple Image
**Sample Payload for Image gen**
```json
{
  "templates": [
    {
      "templateType": "simple_image",
      "templateParams": {
        "ImageDescription": "Prompt to Generate Image",
        "VariationCount": 2,
        "EnhancePrompt": true,
        "AspectRatio": "banner_w2048_h512"
      }
    }
  ],
  "workflowName": "Generate First Image",
  "requestContext": {} // You can flow any context information that you want to find in the Monitor API response.
}
```
**Sample Response:**
```json
{
  "message": "Request initiated successfully",
  "monitorId": "ed390b26-4d4f-4a27-a3f8-6225e9e84cdd",
  "links": [
    {
      "rel": "batchJobStatus",
      "href": "https://api-us.typeface.ai/batch-service/accounts/8f71f690-5404-4862-a3e4-0ebd6cfe6b88/projects/1/batch-jobs/ed390b26-4d4f-4a27-a3f8-6225e9e84cdd"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Notes:**

`templateParams.ImageDescription` - Prompt for generating image

`templateParams.VariationCount` - Number of variations to generate

`templateParams.Layout` - **(Optional)** An identifier for a layout which can be used in *simple_image* template flow.

**Layout** value can be obtained by making an API call to fetch Layout details, and capturing the `ref` field in response.  The API to fetch available layouts is documented [here](https://developers.typeface.ai/reference/querylayoutmanifestsinproject)

`templateParams.Assets` - **(Optional)** A list of asset identifiers. For `simple_image` template flow, only a single image asset identifier is allowed.

**Assets** value can be obtained by making an API call to fetch Asset details, and capturing the `ref` field in response.  The API to fetch available assets is documented [here](https://developers.typeface.ai/reference/queryassetsinproject)


`templateParams.AudienceSegment` - **(Optional)** An identifier for audience to generate personalized content for specific users.

**AudienceSegment** value can be obtained by making an API call to list Audiences, and capturing the `ref` field in response. The API to fetch available audiences is documented [here](https://developers.typeface.ai/reference/queryaudiencesinaccount)

`templateParams.BrandKitImageStyle` - **(Optional)** An identifier for image style in Brand Kit to generate personalized content for specific brands.

**BrandKitImageStyle** value can be obtained by making an API call to fetch Brand Kit image style details, and capturing the `ref` field in response.  The API to fetch available image styles is documented [here](https://developers.typeface.ai/reference/getstyleinbrandkit)

`templateParams.BrandKitTextStyle` - **(Optional)** An identifier for text style in Brand Kit to generate personalized content for specific brands.

**BrandKitTextStyle** value can be obtained by making an API call to fetch Brand Kit text style details, and capturing the `ref` field in response.  The API to fetch available text styles is documented [here](https://developers.typeface.ai/reference/getstyleinbrandkit)

`templateParams.EnhancePrompt` - true/false. Enhances the user prompt if specified as true.

`templateparams.AspectRatio` - **(Optional)** Determines the aspect ratio for generated images. Allowed values are:
-    `square_w768_h768` (Square 768x768)
-    `square_w1024_h1024` (Square 1024x1024)
-    `landscape_w768_h576` (Landscape 768x576)
-    `landscape_w1024_h768` (Landscape 1024x768)
-    `portrait_w576_h768` (Portrait 576x768)
-    `portrait_w768_h1024` (Portrait 768x1024)
-    `widescreen_w1024_h576` (Widescreen 1024x576)
-    `banner_w2048_h512` (Banner 2048x512)

**Note**:  `AspectRatio` should not be used in conjunction with `Layout` field. To define the  aspect ratio with a Logo, the desired aspect ratio can be added via the typeface.ai Web User Interface.

`workflowName` - This will be deprecated, for now flow any label/random number.

`requestContext` - Any additional information (JSON) client wants to receive as part of polling API response.

---
## Simple Text
**Sample Payload for Text gen**
```json
{
  "templates": [
    {
      "templateType": "simple_text",
      "templateParams": {
        "Prompt": "Prompt to Generate Text"
      }

```
**Notes:**

`templateParams.AudienceSegment` - **(Optional)** An identifier for audience to generate personalized content for specific users.

**AudienceSegment** value can be obtained by making an API call to list Audiences, and capturing the `ref` field in response. The API to fetch available audiences is documented [here](https://developers.typeface.ai/reference/queryaudiencesinaccount)

`templateParams.BrandKitImageStyle` - **(Optional)** An identifier for image style in Brand Kit to generate personalized content for specific brands.

**BrandKitImageStyle** value can be obtained by making an API call to fetch Brand Kit image style details, and capturing the `ref` field in response.  The API to fetch available image styles is documented [here](https://developers.typeface.ai/reference/getstyleinbrandkit)

## Email
**Sample Payload for Email**
```json
{
  "templates": [
    {
      "templateType": "email",
      "templateParams": {
        "Purpose": "recruit for a new role",
        "Context": "I am recruiting for a senior marketing manager role for my company",
        "FollowUpResponse": "share what time they are available for a meeting"
      }
    }
  ],
  "workflowName": "Generate an Email",
  "requestContext": {} // You can flow any context information that you want to find in the Monitor API response.
}
```
**Notes:**

`templateParams.Purpose` - The main objective or reason for sending the email. This could be to inform, request information, follow up on a previous conversation, schedule a meeting, confirm details, or provide updates.

`templateParams.Context` - The background information and circumstances related to the email. This includes any relevant details that help the recipient understand the reason for the email and its importance.

`templateParams.FollowUpResponse` - The anticipated or requested action that the recipient should take after reading the email. This could be replying with specific information, confirming receipt, providing feedback, scheduling a meeting, or any other response that moves the conversation or process forward.

`templateParams.Assets` - **(Optional)** A list of asset identifiers. For `email` template flow, only file asset identifiers are allowed.

**Assets** value can be obtained by making an API call to fetch Asset details, and capturing the `ref` field in response.  The API to fetch available assets is documented [here](https://developers.typeface.ai/reference/queryassetsinproject)

`templateParams.AudienceSegment` - **(Optional)** An identifier for audience to generate personalized content for specific users.

post.description:
A unified API to search for assets within a team (and Organization) using various filters.

This API serves as both listing and search endpoint, listing behavior will return results immediately while search behaviour
returns results in a eventual consistent manner, waits for the results to be indexed. Simillarly the updates and deletes are 
also eventually consistent.


Asset sub types for mapped are as follows
| General Usage | Asset Sub Type |
|---|---|
| Uploaded Image | IMAGE |
| Generated Image | GENERATED_IMAGE |
| Uploaded File | FILE |
| Generated Document | GENERATED_DOCUMENT |

**Notes:**
- To retrive SVG images along with other images pass mediaType in the payload with 
  value of `["DEFAULT", "GRAPHIC_SVG"]`

#### Sample Image search request payload with both query and tags filtering
```json
{
  "query": "A red car on the beachside",
  "assetType": "IMAGE",
  "assetSubTypes": ["IMAGE", "GENERATED_IMAGE"],
  "tags": ["vacation", "beach"],
  "limit": 20,
  "cursor": ".....",
  "mediaTypes": ["DEFAULT", "GRAPHIC_SVG"]
}
```

```json
{
  "query": "A scenic view of mountains during sunrise",
  "assetType": "IMAGE",
  "assetSubTypes": ["IMAGE", "GENERATED_IMAGE"],
  "limit": 20,

```

#### Filter by tags
Use the `tags` array to filter assets by one or more tag names. Tag filtering is hierarchical.
When you filter by a parent tag, assets tagged with any of its descendants are automatically included.

For example, given the tag hierarchy `marketing` → `social_media` → `instagram`, filtering by
`marketing` returns assets tagged with `marketing`, `social_media`, or `instagram`.
```json
{
  "assetType": "IMAGE",
  "assetSubTypes": ["IMAGE", "GENERATED_IMAGE"],
  "tags": ["marketing"],
  "limit": 20,
  "cursor": ".....",
  "mediaTypes": ["DEFAULT", "GRAPHIC_SVG"]
}
```

You can also filter by a tag at any level in the hierarchy. For example, filtering by `social_media`
returns assets tagged with `social_media` or `instagram`, but not those only tagged with `marketing`.
```json
{
  "assetType": "IMAGE",
  "assetSubTypes": ["IMAGE", "GENERATED_IMAGE"],
  "tags": ["social_media"],
  "limit": 20,
  "cursor": ".....",
  "mediaTypes": ["DEFAULT", "GRAPHIC_SVG"]
}
```

path.description:
The field to update.
